column2: I'd be interested to hear an opinion from Anthropic on this; there are two angles: why would they make content-related decisions going beyond any lawful use, and second, wouldn't this specific issue be antithetical to how LLMs work? Training frontier models was effectively the single largest instance of piracy in human history. I'm not passing judgement on whether that is good or bad, just calling it what it is, and saying that re-creations are objectively less controversial than that.

Is there any calculation/projection/cost-benefit done on the effects of these measures? I did not renew my Google AI sub because Gemini started to reject transcribing song lyrics due to IP. This seems like a similar thing

The entire issue with this is the dmca and not being able to share what is RE’d from the US.

So much more would be possible were this the case.

That being said… I’m not sure it should be illegal to share this re’d code.

And at the very least … just take it and rewrite what it does in rust lol.

Might not be clean room but hell, if it works.

I’ve gotten good mileage out of binary patching in trampolines lol

And adding in kernel shims.

The only part that’s missing that would probably help is tossing in more storage and moving logs off of root lol.

Open-weight models are close. Claude is very good, but the others aren't far behind. The [cybersecurity] [cyber] alerts are annoying enough we looked for other options. Kimi and GLM have been very capable working with Ghidra, but I haven't tried REA yet
And this, gives their competitors the edge in this regard, it doesn't stop it from happening.
